en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.19.
Atītattika (The Triplet on the Past)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition. A present state is a condition for a present state by way of root condition—the present roots.
It is a condition, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*), for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*) ... [etc] ...
Object:
A past state is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*), for a present state—having given a gift, having observed virtue...
Having undertaken the observance-day practice... [as before] ...he reviews it; he reviews past deeds well-performed;
having emerged from jhāna, he reviews the jhāna. Noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, review the fruit, review the defilements abandoned, and review the defilements suppressed.
They know the defilements previously practiced. One contemplates the past eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self … [and so on] … grief arises.

One contemplates the past ear … nose … tongue … body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangible objects … the physical base … and the past aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
One contemplates it, relishes it, and delights in it; with that as its object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and grief arises.
The base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness by way of object-condition.
The base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object-condition. [The same applies to] the past...

The aggregates are related to the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power, the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their karma,
and to advertence, by way of object condition.
A future state is related to a present state by way of object condition— for example, the future eye.
...pe... the physical basis ... future aggregates as impermanent ... pe ... sorrow arises.

Future aggregates are related to knowledge of supernormal powers (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*), knowledge of others' minds (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*), knowledge of the future (*anāgataṃsa-ñāṇa*), and advertence (*āvajjanā*) by way of object condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
A present state is related to a present state by way of object condition—a present ...
The eye … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical basis [of mind] … one contemplates the present aggregates as impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises;

one sees a visible form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element; the visible-form base is the object-condition for eye-consciousness … the tangible-base is the object-condition for body-consciousness.
...pe... Present aggregates are related to the knowledge of supernormal powers and to advertence by way of object-condition.
Predominance:
A past state is related to a present state by way of predominance-condition. Object-predominance: [For example,] a gift...
Having given and undertaken the precepts …pe… one reflects with reverence upon things well-performed in the past;
having emerged from jhāna, one reflects with reverence upon the jhāna. Noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect with reverence upon the path and reflect with reverence upon the fruit.
[One reflects with reverence upon] the past eye …pe… body … forms … sounds … smells … [tastes … tangibles … mental objects].
… tastes … tangibles … the physical basis … having made past aggregates an object of esteem, one relishes them and delights in them;
with that as an object of esteem, lust arises, wrong view arises.
A future state is a condition for a present state by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): the future...
The eye … [and so on] … the physical basis … one esteems, relishes, and delights in future aggregates;
esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises.
A present state is a condition for a present state by way of predominance-condition (adhipatipaccaya): namely, object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati).
Conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: one esteems, relishes, and delights in the present eye … [and so on] … the physical basis;
esteeming them, lust arises, wrong view arises.
Conascence-predominance: present predominance [is related] to its associated aggregates and to mind-produced [matter].
[It is] a condition for visible forms by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
A past state is a condition for a present state by way of the proximity condition (*anantarapaccaya*): the preceding preceding past [states].
The preceding aggregates are a condition for the succeeding present aggregates by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage; adaptation is a condition for purification; change-of-lineage is a condition for the Path; purification is a condition for the Path;
the Path is a condition for the Fruit; the Fruit is a condition for the Fruit; adaptation is a condition for the attainment of fruition; and for one emerging from cessation...
The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of proximity-condition (*anantarapaccaya*).
Immediate:
A past state is a condition for a present state by way of immediate-condition (*samanantarapaccaya*). (This is the same as the [section on] proximity.)
A present state that is co-nascent, etc., is a condition for a present state by way of co-nascence condition … by way of mutuality condition … by way of support condition. (Abbreviated.
Decisive Support.
A past state is a condition for a present state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*):
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … [as appropriate] … Natural decisive support:
relying on past faith, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha duty, arouses jhāna, and develops insight.
...the path ... supernormal knowledge ... or an attainment; he arouses conceit and adopts wrong views.
Depending upon past virtue ... pe ... wisdom ... lust ... pe ... aspiration ... bodily pleasure ...
or bodily pain, one gives a gift, undertakes precepts, performs the Uposatha duties ... pe ... arouses an attainment, or kills a living being.
...pe... one causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Past faith ... pe ... wisdom; lust ... pe ... aspiration;
bodily pleasure ... bodily pain; [these are] related to present faith ... pe ... wisdom, to lust ... pe ...
aspiration, and to the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
A future state is a condition for a present state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—
namely, as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [and so on] … As natural decisive support:
aspiring for the attainment of future eye-faculty … ear-faculty … nose-faculty … tongue-faculty … body-faculty … beauty … sound … fragrance … [and so forth].
… desiring excellence of taste … desiring excellence of tangible objects … [and so on] … desiring future aggregates,

one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha duties … future excellence of the eye … [and so on] … excellence of complexion … [and so on] … excellence of tangible objects … future aggregates [are related] to present faith … [and so on] … to wisdom, and to bodily …
[It is] a condition for pleasure, bodily pain, the Path, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A present state is a condition for a present state by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) …pe….
As natural decisive support: depending on a present temperature, one arouses jhāna.
Insight … [and so on] … depending upon present food and lodging, one arouses jhāna … [and so on] … one arouses attainment.
Present temperature, food, and lodging are related to present faith … [and so on] … wisdom,
to bodily [well-being] … [and so on] … to the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition.
A pre-arisen present state is a condition for a present state by way of the pre-arisen condition—namely, objective pre-arising and physical-basis pre-arising.
Objective pre-arising: the eye … [and so on] … [contemplating] the physical basis as impermanent … [and so on] … [arises] grief.
[One] arises; one sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element.

The visible-form base is a pre-arising condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-object base is a pre-arising condition for body-consciousness. As for the pre-arising condition of the physical basis:
the eye-base is a pre-arising condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base is a pre-arising condition for body-consciousness.
The [heart-]base is a condition for present aggregates by way of the prenascence condition.

Postnascent Condition: A present state is a condition for a present state by way of the postnascence condition—the postnascence of present aggregates is a condition for this prenascent body by way of the postnascence condition.
A past state is a condition for a present state by way of the condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya):
preceding past aggregates are a condition for succeeding present aggregates by way of the condition of repetition.

Adaptation is related to change-of-lineage; adaptation is related to purification; change-of-lineage is related to the path; purification is related to the path by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).
[Kamma]...

A past state is a condition for a present state by way of kamma-condition. As asynchronous: past volition is a condition for present resultant aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma (kaṭattā-rūpa) by way of kamma-condition.
A present state is a condition for a present state by way of kamma-condition:
present volition is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking...
Present volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for its associated aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*).
[Resultant Condition: A present state that is resultant is a condition, by way of resultant-condition, for a present state—a present resultant...

One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition … pe … two aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of resultant condition.
Nutriment, etc. (Āhārādi).

A present state is a condition for a present state by way of nutriment-condition … faculty-condition … jhāna-condition … path-condition … association-condition … dissociation-condition—[namely] conascent, prenascent, and postnascent. [As to] conascent: present [states]…

Aggregates are related to mind-produced matter by way of dissociation condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, present aggregates are related to kamma-produced matter by way of dissociation condition;
aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of dissociation condition; the physical basis is related to aggregates by way of dissociation condition. As for prenascence: the eye-base...
The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness;

the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition for present aggregates by way of dissociation-condition (vippayutta-paccaya). Subsequently arisen present aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen body by way of dissociation-condition.
There is a present state that is a condition for a present state by way of the presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*). (This is similar to the "existence" [condition] in the "arisen" triad.
Non-existence, disappearance, and non-disappearance.
A past state is a condition for a present state by way of the non-existence condition … and by way of the disappearance condition.
A present state is a condition for a present state by way of the non-disappearance condition … [and so on].
Chapter on Enumeration.
In the pure root condition, one; in the object condition, three; in the predominance condition, three; in the proximity condition, one; in the contiguity condition, one;
in the conascence, mutuality, dependence, and support conditions, one; in the decisive support condition, three; in the prenascence, postnascence, repetition, and kamma conditions, one.
Two [factors] are resultant; one is nutriment …pe… one is non-disappearance. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive order.
Negative extraction.

A past state is a condition for a present state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*), and by way of kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*).
A future state is a condition for a present state by way of object-condition and by way of decisive support-condition.
A present state is a condition for a present state by way of object-condition and by way of conascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*).
Condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition … by way of postnascence condition … by way of nutriment condition … by way of faculty condition.
1.19.7.2. Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya)
In the Enumeration Chapter,
under the Pure [Dependent Condition], there are three for not-root, three for not-object, three for not-predominance, three for not-proximity … pe … three for not-association.
Three with non-dissociation, two with non-presence, three with non-absence, three with non-disappearance, and two with non-non-disappearance.
(Thus it should be counted.
The Negative (Paccanīya).

1.19.7.3. Positive-Negative Conditionality (Paccayānulomapaccanīya) With root condition (hetupaccaya), there is one [instance] for not-object (na-ārammaṇa); one for not-predominance (na-adhipati), not-proximity (na-anantara), not-contiguity (na-samanantara), not-mutuality (na-aññamañña), not-strong-dependence (na-upanissaya)… pe … not-association (na-sampayutta), not-dissociation (na-vippayutta), not-absence (na-atthi), and not-disappearance (na-vigata). (Thus it should be counted.
Positive-Negative Conditionality.
1.19.7.4. Positive Converse of Conditions (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma) With the non-root condition (nahetupaccaya),
there are three [results] for the object condition (ārammaṇa), three for the predominance condition (adhipati), one each for the proximity, contiguity, conascence, mutuality,

and support conditions (anantara, samanantara, sahajāta, aññamañña, nissaya), three for the decisive support condition (upanissaya), one each for the prenascence, postnascence, and repetition conditions (purejāta, pacchājāta, āsevana) …pe… [and] for the kamma condition (kamma).
Two [factors] are resultant; one [factor] is resultant (in these sections, it is only one); one [factor] is non-disappearance. (Thus they should be counted.
Negative-Positive.
Chapter on Questions.
The triad of the past is finished.
